en: The *Ullambana Sūtra* translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Fahu of the Yuezhi during the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park. Great...
Maudgalyāyana had just attained the six supernormal powers and, wishing to deliver his parents to repay the kindness of their nursing, he used his eye of the Path to survey the world.
He saw that his deceased mother had been reborn among the hungry ghosts, unable to see food or drink, her skin and bones standing together in emaciation.
Maudgalyāyana was filled with sorrow; he immediately filled his alms bowl with rice and went to provide food for his mother.
When his mother received the bowl of rice, she shielded it with her left hand while grasping at the rice with her right.
Before the food had even entered his mouth, it transformed into glowing coals, so that he was unable to eat.
Maudgalyāyana cried out loudly, wailing and weeping in grief; he hurried back to inform the Buddha, reporting everything exactly as it had occurred.
The Buddha said:
"Your mother's roots of sin are deep and firmly entangled; they are beyond what you alone can overcome!

Though your filial piety moves heaven and earth, neither the celestial deities, the terrestrial deities, the malevolent spirits, the heretics, the Daoist masters, nor the gods of the Four Heavenly Kings can do anything about it!"
One must rely upon the majestic spiritual power of the Saṃgha of the ten directions to attain liberation.
I shall now explain for you the method of deliverance, so that all beings in distress may be freed from sorrow and suffering, and their karmic obstructions eliminated.
The Buddha told Maudgalyāyana:

"On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when the Sangha observes the *pravāraṇā* ceremony, one should, for the sake of parents of seven generations past and those currently facing hardships and calamities, prepare meals, foods of a hundred flavors, the five fruits, basins for water, oil lamps, beds, mats, and bedding—setting all the world’s delicacies within these vessels—and offer them to the assembly of virtuous monks of the ten directions."
On this day, all the holy assembly—some were in mountain retreats practicing dhyāna-concentration, some had attained the fruits of the four paths, and some were walking in meditation beneath trees;
some possessed mastery of the six supernormal powers and were teaching śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
others were great bodhisattvas of the ten stages who had manifested as bhikṣus among the great multitude.
All with one mind, they partake of the *pātra-bhara* meal.

Possessing the path of the noble assembly of those endowed with pure precepts, their virtue is vast and boundless. Any who make offerings to such monks during the *pravāraṇā* ceremony shall cause their present parents, parents of seven generations past, and six kinds of relatives to escape the sufferings of the three evil realms; they shall attain liberation at that very moment, and clothing and food shall appear spontaneously.
Furthermore, if there are those whose parents are still living, they shall enjoy blessings and happiness for a hundred years;

if their parents of the past seven generations have already passed away, they shall be reborn in heaven, born spontaneously by transformation, entering the radiant light of celestial flowers, and experience immeasurable bliss.

At that time, the Buddha commanded the assembly of monks from the ten directions: "First, on behalf of the donors' families, recite incantations for the seven generations of ancestors; then, practice the mind of meditative concentration before receiving food."
When first receiving the alms bowl, one should first place it before the Buddha stupa; once the assembly of monks has finished their incantations and prayers, one may then receive the food oneself.
At that time, the bhikṣu Maudgalyāyana and the great assembly of bodhisattvas were all filled with great joy, and Maudgalyāyana’s weeping and sobbing were completely stilled.
At that time, on that very day, Maudgalyāyana’s mother was liberated from the suffering of a hungry ghost for one kalpa.
Then Maudgalyāyana again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"My parents, who gave me birth, have been able to receive the power of the merit of the Triple Gem and the majestic spiritual power of the Sangha."

Therefore, if all disciples of the Buddha in future ages who practice filial piety likewise offer this *bowl-of-liberation* (*ulambana-patra*) to rescue and deliver their present parents, as well as their parents up to the seventh generation, would this not be appropriate?
The Buddha said:
"Excellent and most skillful is your question!
It was precisely what I intended to speak of, yet you have asked about it now."
"Good son!

If there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs, kings, crown princes, princes, ministers, high officials, the three dukes, the hundred officials, or the myriad commoners who practice filial piety and compassion, they should all, for the sake of their present parents and their parents of the past seven generations, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month—the day when the Buddha rejoices and the day of the Saṃgha’s *pravāraṇā*—place food and drink of a hundred flavors within an *urndabhaṇa* vessel and offer it to the *pravāraṇā*-observing monks of the ten directions. They should then make this aspiration: 'May our present parents live for a hundred years, free from illness and all suffering and affliction; may our parents of the past seven generations be liberated from the sufferings of the hungry ghosts and be reborn among devas and humans, enjoying boundless merit and happiness.'"
The Buddha addressed the sons and daughters of good family:

"Those disciples of the Buddha who cultivate filial piety should, in every moment of thought, constantly remember their parents and make offerings to them, even up to their parents for seven generations."

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month every year, one should always, with filial piety and compassionate remembrance, honor one's living parents and even those up to seven generations of ancestors by making offerings of the *bowl-of-liberation* (*urabon*) to the Buddhas and the Sangha, thereby repaying the kindness of their long-term nurturing and loving care.
"If all disciples of the Buddha should uphold this Dharma.
At that time, the bhikṣu Maudgalyāyana and the fourfold assembly of disciples, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Scripture on the Ullambana Sutra Spoken by the Buddha
